answer: A practical sybil defence ties reputation to verifiable work over time, not to a free account. Think of trust as a trellis that only grows where it is tended: completed tasks, on-chain attestations, and peer endorsements accumulate slowly, while a fresh island of fake identities starts with no history. When a sudden tide of new accounts tries to flood a vote or reward pool, the system weights proven history more heavily and rate-limits newcomers, so cheap copies buy little influence.
